Hi Amanda — thanks for sending this over and for flagging the timeline. I've attached a concise SLO summary that addresses the team's common procurement points.

Quick notes up front:
- We publish our composite availability SLOs (regional) and a suite of latency SLIs (p50/p95/p99 request token latency). We separate client-side network transit time from server inference time in our telemetry by tagging span start/stop at the API gateway and at the inference host.
- Rolling windows: we use 5m/1h/24h aggregations for realtime alerting and 30d/sliding windows for monthly SLO reports.
- We can provide read-only Grafana access scoped to your account and a limited telemetry export for procurement review.
- Exception path: for burst or degradation events we have an incident classification and SLO exception playbook; credits and formal remediation are handled via the procurement SLA addendum (draft attached).

Marissa & Ben — can you confirm the proposed Grafana invite flow and the exact telemetry exports we can share (sanitized)? Also please add any detail on alert routing and on how we document client vs server latency.

Sofia — adding technical detail for Amanda's team. Quoting Amanda's key asks below for context.

On 2027-05-20 09:12 Amanda Lee wrote:
> - Exact SLIs used to measure uptime and token latency (how are client-side vs server-side latencies separated?)

Answers:
- SLIs: availability (successful response rate) measured per-region at the API gateway (successful status codes / total requests), and latency SLIs measured on server-side inference completion for common model families. We provide p50/p95/p99 and a trimmed-mean for burst-resistant reporting.
- Client vs server: every request carries two spans: gateway-accept and inference-complete. Gateway-accept -> gateway-respond captures ingress/egress; gateway-accept -> inference-complete isolates server processing. We also capture kernel-level queue times on GPUs to help correlate queuing vs model compute.
- Measurement windows: realtime alerting uses a 5m sliding window, cadence reports use 1h and 24h; monthly SLO calculations use a 30-day rolling window with business-hours and 24/7 variants selectable per contract.
- Alerting: Default thresholds we recommend: p95 latency > 900ms (for standard models) or a 3% availability drop sustained over 15m. Alerts route to Redwood on-call + customer SRE email (we can add your pager/Slack). We support webhook and PagerDuty integrations.
- Dashboards/exports: we can provision a read-only Grafana board scoped to Greenleaf with the following panels: regional availability, p95/p99 latency by model, request-rate heatmap, error taxonomy. For procurement review we provide a one-time raw telemetry export (CSV/Parquet) filtered to remove customer payloads and PII.
- Exception handling: We classify events as transient (<30m), sustained (30m–6h), and major incident (>6h). Exception requests for credit require: incident report, SLO impact calc, root-cause analysis, and remediation plan. Credits are pro-rated per contract terms in the SLA addendum.

Let me know if you want specific sample queries (PromQL) or a short runbook extract. Happy to assemble.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Reliability & Observability, Redwood Inference
